trade.text: She called for removing tariffs on critical farm inputs to lower costs.
trade.quote: Remove tariffs on critical farm inputs to lower costs.

housing.text: She supports investing in affordable housing so people can live and work in their communities.
housing.quote: Investing in affordable housing, infrastructure, broadband, and community development so South Dakotans can live and work in the communities they call home.

schools.text: She opposed proposed federal cuts to public education and urged lawmakers to reject the House bill.
schools.quote: These draconian cuts to public education put the future of South Dakota’s children on the line. $18 million in cuts to South Dakota’s public education will reduce staffing, increase classroom sizes, and provide fewer programs to our children.

immigration.text: She said Congress should consider an immigration bill that provides a citizenship opportunity for people who arrived on work visas.
immigration.quote: I know a lot of people would like to see an opportunity for citizenship for those who came here on a work visa.

abortion.text: Her candidate profile says she supports women making reproductive-health-care decisions with their doctors.
abortion.quote: Protecting a woman’s ability to make her own reproductive health care decisions in consultation with her doctor.

health.text: She supports protecting Medicare and Medicaid and expanding Medicare funding for nursing homes.
health.quote: We can make health care affordable by protecting Medicare, Medicaid, and restoring the Marketplace tax credits that keep private market coverage in reach for thousands of South Dakotans.

voting.text: She opposed new mail-ballot restrictions and said eligible voters should face fewer barriers to participation.
voting.quote: We should be making it easier, not harder, for eligible South Dakotans to participate in our elections.

tax.text: He says he will support cutting taxes as part of the Trump agenda.
tax.quote: President Trump endorsed me, and I support his agenda. Secure the border, cut taxes, and put America first.

safety.text: He says he will back police, sheriffs, and prosecutors and puts public safety first.
safety.quote: In Congress I will back our police, sheriffs, and prosecutors with the tools and the respect they have earned. Public safety comes first.

immigration.text: He calls for securing the border, finishing the wall, and letting law enforcement do its job.
immigration.quote: The meth and fentanyl on our streets come across an open border. I have prosecuted the traffickers who bring it here. Secure the border, finish the wall, and let law enforcement do its job.

guns.text: He says the right to bear arms is nonnegotiable and pledges to defend the Second Amendment.
guns.quote: The right to keep and bear arms is not negotiable. I hunt, I raised my kids around firearms handled right, and I have an A+ rating from the NRA. I will defend the Second Amendment every time.

abortion.text: As attorney general, he ordered a company to stop advertising abortion pills in South Dakota and said the state could sue if it did not comply.
abortion.quote: South Dakota Attorney General Marty Jackley has sent a letter to Mayday Health ordering the company to immediately cease and desist the deceptive advertising of the sale of abortion pills in South Dakota

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He said men should not play on women’s sports teams and pledged to protect women athletes under that approach.
gender.quote: “I have long advocated that men should not be allowed to play in women sports,” said Attorney General Jackley. “South Dakota is one of 27 states not to allow men to play on women’s sports teams. I am committed to protecting the women student-athletes competing at South Dakota universities.”
